req.title: Login case-sensitive username
req.statement: The system shall treat usernames as case-sensitive on POST /auth/login.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that usernames are case-sensitive on POST /auth/login. The flaskr auth.login view performs a direct SQL equality match on username (SELECT * FROM user WHERE username = ?), so 'Rahul' and 'rahul' are distinct. Tests must verify: (1) exact-case login succeeds with HTTP 302 redirect, (2) wrong-case login fails with HTTP 200 and error message, (3) boundary: single-character case difference at the first character. Pre-loaded DB has user 'Rahul'/'stone', 'Anjali'/'cloud', 'Ishaan'/'stone'. We use these exact credentials. Mutation resilience: assert exact status codes (302 vs 200), exact redirect location, exact error text, and both sides of the case-sensitivity comparison.

tests.name: test_login_exact_case_succeeds
preconditions: Database contains user with username='Rahul' and password='stone'
Application is in TESTING mode with a fresh database
trace: R-FLASKR-036: exact-case username must authenticate successfully
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os
from flaskr.db import init_db

def test_login_exact_case_succeeds():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'
    os.unlink(path)

test_login_exact_case_succeeds()

from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os
from flaskr.db import init_db

def test_login_boundary_single_char_case_difference():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r_wrong = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'ishaan', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert r_wrong.status_code == 200
    assert b'Incorrect username.' in r_wrong.data
    r_correct = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Ishaan', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert r_correct.status_code == 302
    assert r_correct.headers['Location'] == '/'
    os.unlink(path)

test_login_boundary_single_char_case_difference()

from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os
from flaskr.db import init_db

def test_login_correct_case_redirects_to_index_not_login():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Diya', 'password': 'cloud'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    location = r.headers['Location']
    assert location == '/'
    assert location != '/auth/login'
    os.unlink(path)
